Thanks again for submitting the initial SIG package. During our intake review we have a few follow-ups focused on key encryption key (KEK) transportation provenance and retention for tenant envelope keys. Specifically we need:

- Evidence of HSM attestation for the devices used in the last 18 months (FIPS level and vendor statement).
- The retention/archival policy and sample retention artifact (how long you keep KEK wrapping metadata and who can access it).
- Any procedures and logs showing secure wipe/evacuation of ephemerals in the event of rekey or decommission.

Our auditor wants these by EOD 2029-03-08 to keep the SIG timeline. Can your team provide the above or indicate gaps? If some items are restricted, please flag what we can redact (we will accept redacted operator IDs in the manifest if necessary).

Hi Lydia —

Appreciate the clear list. We can provide a transport manifest and HSM attestation artifacts; some raw operator identifiers are treated as internal and we typically provide redacted operator IDs in customer-facing artifacts. High level answers up front:

- Transport manifest: yes — we maintain a manifest that records each KEK movement, including wrap/unwrap events, source/destination HSM serials, UTC timestamps, and operator identifiers (we can provide redacted IDs).
- HSM attestation: yes — FIPS module/attestation statements for the HSM fleet are available (we’ll include vendor PDFs).
- Retention: KEK wrapping metadata is retained for 7 years by default to support audits; access is limited to the Crypto Ops group via RBAC enforced through our IAM and audited in our logging pipeline.
- Wipe/evacuation: we have documented wipe procedures and a sample execution log (ephemeral keys are zeroized on decommission and verified by a two-operator approval flow).

I’m looping in Marissa (crypto ops) to assemble the artifacts; Jonas will include operator access logs and Ben can confirm retention policy language for the SIG template. Expect an initial package tomorrow morning (2029-03-06). If possible, let me know which format your auditor prefers for manifests (CSV, PDF manifest, or JSON).
